condition: Syncope from complete heart block (elderly, on a beta-blocker)
summary: 83-year-old woman with two blackouts without warning this week, on bisoprolol: HR 34 regular, BP 118/50. ESC 2018: bradycardia <40 bpm with syncope is high risk.

inputs.hpi: Follow-up after femoral hernia repair. Daughter reports two falls this week where she "just went down" without warning, brief loss of consciousness each time, no injury. Tired and breathless on the stairs for a month. Takes bisoprolol for blood pressure.

exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 34 regular, BP 118/50, cannon waves in the JVP.

surgicalHistory: Open femoral hernia repair (4 weeks ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Syncope due to suspected complete heart block
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Recurrent syncope without prodrome with HR 34 - suspected complete heart block; emergency transfer for ECG monitoring and pacing assessment; hold bisoprolol.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Acute Diverticulitis | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis. PANE has no syncope or arrhythmia node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add an ESC 2018 syncope risk rule: syncope during exertion or supine, without prodrome, with chest pain/breathlessness, structural heart disease, HR <40 or SBP <90 -> urgent/emergency with ECG and echo; typical reflex prodrome with none of these -> routine.

It appears only as plan text: "• 12-lead ECG — P-wave morphology, PR interval, heart block grade." (web.clinicalPrompts); "• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40)." mustInclude.proposedFix: A prompt already offers this as plan text ("• 12-lead ECG — P-wave morphology, PR interval, heart block grade."): emit it as an addToInvestigations action so it reaches the investigation list.

mustExclude.note: No PE features; checks the iOS radiation-card substring match ("pe" in "syncope"/"suspected").

guideline.name: 2018 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope
guideline.section: Table 5 risk stratification: high-risk - syncope during exertion or supine, absence of prodrome, new chest discomfort/breathlessness, structural heart disease, ECG with Mobitz II or third-degree AV block or bradycardia <40 bpm, unexplained SBP <90 mmHg, GI bleeding; low-risk - typical reflex prodrome and triggers; low-risk patients discharged, high-risk patients need early intensive evaluation; brain imaging not recommended in uncomplicated syncope
guideline.citation: Brignole M, Moya A, de Lange FJ, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:1883-1948.

rationale: Elderly permutation: "falls" rather than "syncope", on a rate-limiting drug. The web bradycardia vital cascade should fire; this checks triage and the iOS text path.
